title: XAI-TRIS: Non-linear image benchmarks to quantify false positive post-hoc attribution of feature importance
reasoning: The paper focuses on the technical correctness and reliability of XAI methods in identifying truly important features, and the risks of misinterpretations in critical applications. While it discusses the implications for trustworthiness and correct conclusions in high-stakes fields (like medical diagnosis), it does not evaluate or benchmark religion, morals, or ethics as a core component or subject of study. The 'bias' discussed is technical (false-positive attribution of importance), not societal or ethical bias in the typical sense.
